<a id="files-health-and-auxiliary-services"></a>
## Files, health, and auxiliary services

These surfaces are mounted outside the generated Express `/api` route catalogue. The `/files` root is mounted by the same Node process; the health and hardware services are separate processes.

### Express health check

`GET /api/health` is public and has no query parameters or request body. It runs `SELECT 1` with a three-second timeout. A healthy database returns HTTP 200:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "status": "ok",
    "service": "mahali-light",
    "time": "2026-09-21T08:00:00.000Z",
    "database": "up"
  }
}
```

An unreachable or timed-out database returns HTTP 503 with the same shape, `success:false`, `status:"degraded"`, and `database:"unreachable"`. The maintenance middleware runs before this handler; during restore, the current allow-list does not include `/api/health`, so maintenance mode can return the standard 503 `BIZ_MAINTENANCE_MODE` response instead.

### Public and protected file paths

Files are served from the configured uploads root. There is no catch-all uploads endpoint, directory listing, or direct generated-PDF path. The Express route uses `express.static`, so successful reads are ordinary file responses (usually 200; HEAD is also supported by the static middleware), while missing/invalid paths are 404. Authentication and authorization failures use the normal JSON error middleware before a private static mount is reached.

| Method | Path | Access and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/products/:uuid/:filename.webp` | Public. `:uuid` must match a 36-character hexadecimal UUID-shaped path and `:filename` may contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Only `.webp` is accepted. Seven-day static cache headers are used. |
| GET | `/files/store/logo.png` or `/files/store/logo.svg` | Public store logo. Any other `:name` returns plain 404. |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/purchase-orders/*` | Bearer JWT plus `supplier.view`; private, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/supplier-payments/*` | Bearer JWT plus `supplier.view`; private, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/receipts/bills/*` | Bearer JWT plus `bills.view`; private, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/receipts/expenses/*` | Bearer JWT plus `bills.view`; private, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. |
| GET/HEAD | `/files/bug-reports/*` | Bearer JWT plus `bug.view_all`; private, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. |

Dotfiles and directory indexes are denied. Generated invoice, receipt, purchase-order, report, and export documents remain permission-gated through their `/api` endpoints; the file router intentionally does not expose their storage paths.

⚠️ **Implementation Note:** Restore maintenance middleware runs before `/files`, so even public product/logo reads are unavailable while a restore is active.

⚠️ **Implementation Note:** The public product path guard accepts a UUID-shaped string rather than checking that the referenced product exists. Static-file errors after the guard are handled by Express/global error behavior, not by a domain-specific JSON contract. Upload limits and transformations are described on each multipart endpoint in the catalogue: product/variant images are limited to 5 MB, document/receipt attachments to 10 MB, logos to 2 MB, and bug-report screenshots to 2 MB.

### Optional FastAPI ML sidecar

The `backend-fastapi` application is a separate optional service. Its Dockerfile starts Uvicorn on `0.0.0.0:8000`; the source does not mount it under Express and its dormant analytics/forecast Python routers are not registered. The default FastAPI metadata endpoints are also present:

| Method | Path | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/health` | Public; database probe. |
| GET | `/docs` | Public Swagger UI generated by FastAPI. |
| GET | `/redoc` | Public ReDoc UI generated by FastAPI. |
| GET | `/openapi.json` | Public generated OpenAPI document. |

`GET /health` has no parameters, body, authentication, or writes. It returns HTTP 200 even when the sidecar cannot reach PostgreSQL; only the payload changes:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "status": "ok",
    "service": "mahali-ml-future",
    "database": "up",
    "role": "future_ml_only"
  }
}
```

With a failed `SELECT 1`, `status` is `"degraded"` and `database` is `"down"`. No ML business endpoint is currently callable from the checked-out FastAPI application.

### Local hardware print agent

`hardware-agent/server.js` is a separate native Node HTTP service. It binds only to `127.0.0.1`, defaults to port **17473** (`HARDWARE_AGENT_PORT`), and defaults its upstream Express URL to `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (`EXPRESS_URL`). It has no PostgreSQL connection or POS roles; the caller supplies a POS JWT for the upstream PDF request.

| Method | Path | Headers/body | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/health` | None | HTTP 200, `{ "success": true, "data": { "status": "ok", "service": "hardware-agent" } }`. |
| GET | `/v1/printers` | `X-Hardware-Token` must exactly match the local pairing token | HTTP 200, `data` is an array of discovered `{name}` objects. |
| POST | `/v1/print` | `X-Hardware-Token`; JSON body below | HTTP 200, `{ "success": true, "data": { "printed": true } }`. |

The pairing token is a random 32-byte hex string stored at `${HARDWARE_AGENT_DIR || "~/.bytecra-hardware-agent"}/pairing-token`, created with restrictive filesystem permissions. A print request is:

```json
{
  "kind": "invoice",
  "invoiceId": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "apiToken": "<POS JWT used against Express>",
  "printer": "Receipt_Printer",
  "copies": 1
}
```

`kind` must be `invoice` or `receipt`; `invoiceId` must be a UUID; `apiToken` must be a non-empty string; `printer` is passed to the OS print command when supplied; `copies` is coerced and clamped to 1–5 (it is not required to be an integer). The agent fetches `/api/invoices/:id/pdf` or `/api/invoices/:id/receipt` from the configured Express URL, writes a temporary PDF, invokes `lp` on macOS/Linux or the bundled PowerShell print script on Windows, then removes the temporary file.

Important hardware-agent errors are HTTP 400 `HW_BAD_JSON`, `HW_INVALID_PRINT`, or `HW_MISSING_API_TOKEN`; HTTP 401 `HW_UNAUTHORIZED`; HTTP 403 `HW_LOCALHOST_ONLY`; HTTP 404 `HW_UNKNOWN_COMMAND`; HTTP 502 (or the upstream response status) `HW_PRINT_FAILED`; and HTTP 500 `HW_INTERNAL`. The service has no CORS or OPTIONS handler, so browser preflight requests are not supported. Printer discovery is best effort and may return an empty array; on Windows the current parser keeps only the first whitespace-delimited token of a printer name.
